title: A Software-Hardware Co-design Solution for 3D Inner Structure Reconstruction
problem: Volume imaging 3D reconstruction is time-consuming due to poor data locality of the reconstruction algorithm, and complex synchronization presents a major obstacle making ASIC acceleration difficult.
motivation: Volume imaging is critical for medical diagnosis and archaeology applications, with particularly high demand for lung CT imaging during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
method: The approach provides a unified programming model for different 3D reconstruction tasks and redesigns how data flows through the algorithm (the dataflow) to improve data locality—keeping frequently accessed data close together in memory rather than scattered across distant locations. It removes unnecessary coordination points (synchronization) by analyzing which computations actually depend on each other. It then introduces Waffle, a specialized chip architecture that places processing closer to memory (near-memory acceleration), which eliminates the slow data movement that was the original bottleneck.
key_novelty: Waffle is a specialized architecture that accelerates 3D reconstruction by placing processing closer to memory, solving the data locality and synchronization bottlenecks in the algorithm.
contributions: Unified programming model covering various 3D reconstruction tasks
Redesigned dataflow with improved data locality properties
Removal of unnecessary synchronizations through data dependency analysis
Near-memory acceleration architecture (Waffle) achieving 3.5-4× speedup over GPU clusters
